items.rationale: F-TB04 adds qualification catalog and test harnesses only; no alternate production kernel is introduced.
No kernel I/O, parsing, files, units or path behavior is changed.
Cases explicitly separate parameter identity, physical state, forcing, numerical configuration and results through pinned fixture and oracle metadata.
Restart cases preserve compact committed physical continuation state and do not promote immutable parameter payloads into per-column state.
Worker scratch isolation is explicitly catalogued and restart payload checks exclude Newton, Jacobian and warm-start scratch.
MultiSWAP cases exercise serialized and parallel batches without changing production memory layout or execution-class design.
Checkpoint, rejected trial, rollback, retry, stale-candidate and exactly-once commit semantics are permanent qualification targets.
Restart and retry cases preserve committed-origin semantics; trial trajectories are not promoted to physical committed state.
Restart and runtime evidence uses generic committed times and intervals; no day or midnight assumption is introduced.
No coupling-window duration or calendar alignment is introduced or restricted.
Coupling capability remains untouched; transactional and restart testbank coverage is compatible with later coupler qualification.
No SWAP-MODFLOW head or flux interface contract is modified.
Per-column and aggregate water-mass checks retain inherited hard gates; no mass tolerance is relaxed.
No interface-sensitivity contract or response-tangent implementation is changed.
No predictor-corrector run-count or coupling-cost policy is changed.
MultiSWAP is directly represented by one-column, regular, irregular, medium, ordering, worker-count and heterogeneous-parameter-reference cases.
No MODFLOW-cell to SWAP-column cardinality assumption is introduced.
Deep-vadose remains outside SWAP and is unaffected.
No transfer between deep-vadose and direct coupling is implemented or reinterpreted.
The catalog does not hard-code a new soil-water solver; it reuses current qualified authorities through their existing interfaces.
No SWAP physics is duplicated or reimplemented; tests reuse current production contracts and immutable qualification evidence.
No module dependency on HeadCalc internals is added.
Physics, solver policy and determinism requirements remain separate; test profiles do not silently change physical options.
No fallback or bounded-cost production policy is changed; expensive adversarial matrices are confined to RELEASE or DEEP profiles.
Reference-mode authorities remain available and unchanged; F-TB04 does not replace reference qualification.
Cases preserve retries, rejection, commit, restart, worker and mass diagnostics as qualification observables.
Optional-state scaling is explicitly tested so inactive functionality does not require active state or contaminate restart payloads.
Runtime composition relationships remain outside the kernel; F-TB04 changes no tile or coupler ownership.
Fixtures and catalog metadata use explicit authorities and generic time; no hidden file, midnight or MODFLOW dependency is introduced.
F-TB04 records explicit case-to-invariant mapping, validates authority immutability and requires exact-head FAST and RELEASE qualification before the closeout decision is valid.
